y-m-77-01.title: Checking numbers in round-trip speed report
y-m-77-01.topic: Average speed and what average means
y-m-77-01.goal: Calculate to check average round-trip speed may differ from simple mean of two speeds; say when they are equal.
y-m-77-01.material: Delivery driver travels round trip on 12 km one-way route. Outbound 30 km/hour, return 20 km/hour (no stops, constant speed each way). Coworker report reasons as follows.
y-m-77-01.thinking.1: Checking using total-distance and total-time definitions
y-m-77-01.thinking.2: Making several speed pairs meeting conditions
y-m-77-01.prereq.0: Here H3 labels difficulty/support for this production assignment only; it doesn't assign subject to a grade. Assume advanced high-school vocational maths and prior middle-school ratios, percentages, averages and letter expressions.
y-m-77-01.prereq.1: Speed = distance ÷ time; meaning of average (middle school)
y-m-77-01.s.s1.prompt: Choose one line in coworker report unsupported or wrong.
y-m-77-01.s.s1.hint.0: For each line, separate restating problem conditions (distance, speed) from new claim.
y-m-77-01.s.s1.hint.1: Find time going and returning, add them, and compare with report's time.
y-m-77-01.s.s1.line.0: Going: travel 12 km at 30 km per hour.
y-m-77-01.s.s1.line.1: Returning: travel back 12 km at 20 km per hour.
y-m-77-01.s.s1.line.2: Average speed is mean of speeds, so (30+20)÷2 = 25 km/h.
y-m-77-01.s.s1.line.3: Whole 24 km trip at 25 km/h takes 24÷25 = 0.96 hours.
y-m-77-01.s.s1.explain: Lines 1 and 2 just restate conditions, correct. Problem begins line 3: average speed is total distance ÷ total time, but travel times differ; they gave speeds equal weight. Outbound takes 12÷30=0.4 hours, return 12÷20=0.6, total 1 hour; 24 km ÷1=24 km/h. Line 4 uses 25 from line 3, giving wrong 0.96 hours. Whether you selected line 3 or 4 you found error, but source is line 3.
y-m-77-01.s.s2.prompt: Suppose same route has speed a km/h going and b km/h returning. Give two different pairs (a,b) where whole-trip average speed (total distance ÷ total time) is a whole number. a,b distinct natural numbers 10 to 100; one-way distance irrelevant. Exclude example (30,20); (a,b) and (b,a) count same. 10 100 30 20
y-m-77-01.s.s2.hint.0: Set one-way distance to 12 km. For each candidate pair find outbound/return time and add.
y-m-77-01.s.s2.hint.1: For several pairs, table whether total distance ÷ total time is whole number; see what successful pairs share.
y-m-77-01.s.s2.ok.c1: a and b natural numbers 10 to 100.
y-m-77-01.s.s2.fail.c1: Make a and b natural numbers 10 to 100.
y-m-77-01.s.s2.fail.c2: Speeds going and returning must differ.
y-m-77-01.s.s2.ok.c3: This is a new pair of speeds.
y-m-77-01.s.s2.ok.c4: Round-trip average speed is a whole number.
y-m-77-01.s.s2.fail.c4: Round-trip average speed isn't a whole number. Recalculate total distance and time.
y-m-77-01.s.s2.explain: For one-way distance d, time d/a+d/b and average speed 2ab/(a+b). For (60,40) it's 48; (40,10) is 16; (60,30) is 40. Whichever pair, average speed no more than simple mean of speeds. They are equal only when speeds equal. 2 60 40 48 40 10 16 60 30 40
y-m-77-01.s.s3.prompt: Explain to coworker 'why average isn't 25'. Use outbound and return times as evidence, and say when simple mean of speeds is correct.
y-m-77-01.s.s3.hint.0: First write outbound and return times as numbers.
y-m-77-01.s.s3.hint.1: Start by comparing time using 25 (0.96 hours) with actual travel time.
y-m-77-01.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Did you state in your own words that travel times differ?
y-m-77-01.s.s3.selfAssess.1: Did you give numeric value calculated from total distance and total time?
y-m-77-01.s.s3.selfAssess.2: Did you state one condition when simple mean is correct?
y-m-77-01.s.s3.model.0: Average speed is total distance / total time. Outbound 12÷30=0.4 hours, return 12÷20=0.6, total 1 hour; 24 km in 1 hour is 24 km/h. Return leg slower and takes longer, so result isn't 25. Simple mean works if speeds equal or times for both legs equal.
y-m-77-01.s.s3.model.1: At speed 25, 24 km should take 24÷25=0.96 hours, but actual 0.4+0.6=1 hour. More time is spent at slower speed, so average 24, below 25. If both speeds equal, simple mean works.
y-m-77-01.s.s3.modelNote.1: Answers saying simple mean is correct only when speeds are same are accepted too.

y-m-77-03.title: Box packing cost: does one rule always give cheapest price?
y-m-77-03.goal: Use calculation to show 'use as many cheaper-per-item boxes as possible' doesn't guarantee lowest cost for this order; make several packing methods meeting conditions.
y-m-77-03.material: Warehouse ships 100 parts using two box types. Large L holds up to 12 and costs 1,500원; small S holds up to 8 and costs 1,100원. Boxes may have space left, but pack all 100 parts; any number boxes allowed. Employee claims cheapest method below.
